filename: Targeting bias in algorithm optimization improves reconstructions of surface ocean pCO2.pdf
title: Targeting bias in algorithm optimization improves reconstructions of surface ocean pCO2
code_availability: Data analysis scripts and supporting files are publicly available at https://github.com/OceanCarbon-LDEO-Columbia/pCO2Residual_Testbed.
testbed_rationale: Focuses on reconstructing and gap-filling surface ocean pCO2 from sparse observational tracks using observing system simulation experiments, rather than developing or evaluating ML parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Severe observational data sparsity (SOCAT samples only ~2% of global ocean 1°x1° monthly grid cells) and strong regional sampling bias (especially winter Southern Ocean data gaps)
Right-skewed target variable distribution over multidecadal trends (spCO2 increasing over time) causing tree-based algorithms to overestimate early periods and underestimate late periods
Standard MSE/nMSE hyperparameter optimization penalizes large variance rather than systematic drift, exacerbating multiyear negative biases in spCO2 and overestimating the global carbon sink
Varying ESM climate model biases and internal variability when used as testbeds lead to substantial spread in reconstruction error sign and magnitude
extraction_notes: The preprint evaluates hyperparameter tuning criteria (negative MSE vs. bias) for the pCO2-Residual machine learning reconstruction method using XGBoost on a 45-member CMIP6 ensemble testbed and real-world SOCAT observations.
